milestone_description: The proof of Theorem 4.8 chooses a base $B\ge2$ with $8Ng\le B^{m}\le2^{m}\cdot8Ng$ and applies Theorem A.8 to obtain an explicit moment representation with $m$ axes and representation bound $B^{m}$. The milestone states that this instance-independent data (the tables) exists for every verifier with $S\ge2$ assignment coordinates and every gap exponent $\delta<1$.

milestone_title: Theorem 4.8 — the fixed linear system of Construction 4.5 (explicit form)
milestone_description: For a prime $p$, a verifier $V$ with $S$ coordinates and integers $g,m\ge1$, there is a preprocessing reduction from $L(V)$ to block-sparse linear systems over $\mathbb F_p$ with gap $g$ whose matrix has $n\le(8p^{4}m(S+1))^{m+7}g^{1+1/m}$ columns (22). The milestone states this for the linear system of Construction 4.5 itself, for every choice of tables: completeness, soundness with gap $g$, $g<b$, at least one block, and the bound $n^{m}\le(8p^{4}m(S+1))^{(m+7)m}g^{m+1}$.

milestone_title: Lemma 3.12 — the lattice reduction for the paper's lattice (explicit form)
milestone_description: Lemma 3.12 gives a full-rank lattice $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^{M}$ with $2Db\le M<4Db$, integer targets, an integer radius $1\le R\le M$ and a weight $w$ with $w\le16D(\|t-v\|_p/R)^{s}$ for all instances and $w>gD$ for NO instances. The milestone states that these properties hold for the lattice of the proof: the Construction A lattice of the padded code for $p\le2$ and its blockwise Walsh–Hadamard transform for $p>2$ and $p=\infty$, with the radius $\lceil D^{1/p}\rceil$, $\lceil(2^{k}D)^{1/p}\rceil$ or $1$.

milestone_title: Theorem 5.1 (codes) — the paper's code for any quadratic verifier
milestone_description: Theorem 5.1 for codes, with the code named: for every field $F$ of characteristic $p$, every $0<\varepsilon<1$, every quadratic verifier $V$ and every choice of tables, the code $\ker A\times\{0\}$ of the fixed linear system of Construction 4.5 (extended to $F$) with the targets of Lemma 3.11 has block length $M\le(S+1)^{C}$, and $x\in L(V)$ implies $\Delta(t_x,\mathcal C)\le D$ while $x\notin L(V)$ implies $\Delta(t_x,\mathcal C)>M^{1-\varepsilon}\cdot D$, where $D$ is the number of blocks. The milestone is stated for the code and lattice that the paper constructs, so it cannot be met by a construction whose targets depend on the instance in an arbitrary way; polynomial-time computability is not formalized.

milestone_title: Theorem 5.1 (lattices) — the paper's lattice for any quadratic verifier
milestone_description: Theorem 5.1 for lattices, with the lattice named: for every norm exponent $p\ge1$ or $p=\infty$, $s=\min\{p,2\}$, every $0<\varepsilon<1/s$, every quadratic verifier $V$ over $\mathbb F_2$ and every choice of tables, the lattice of Lemma 3.12 for the fixed linear system of Construction 4.5 has full rank and dimension $M\le(S+1)^{C}$, and $x\in L(V)$ implies $\operatorname{dist}_p(t_x,\Lambda)\le R$ while $x\notin L(V)$ implies $\operatorname{dist}_p(t_x,\Lambda)>M^{1/s-\varepsilon}\cdot R$, with the radius $R$ of Lemma 3.12. The milestone is stated for the code and lattice that the paper constructs, so it cannot be met by a construction whose targets depend on the instance in an arbitrary way; polynomial-time computability is not formalized.

milestone_title: Theorem 5.1 (codes, 3SAT) — the paper's code with $M\le n^{C}$
milestone_description: Theorem 5.1 for the nearest codeword problem and the 3SAT verifier, with the code named: for every finite field $F$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$ there is a constant $C$ such that for every number $v\ge1$ of variables there are tables for which the code of the previous milestone has block length $M\le n^{C}$, $n=(2v)^{3}$, and gap $M^{1-\varepsilon}$ between satisfiable and unsatisfiable instances. The milestone is stated for the code and lattice that the paper constructs, so it cannot be met by a construction whose targets depend on the instance in an arbitrary way; polynomial-time computability is not formalized.

milestone_title: Theorem 5.1 (lattices, 3SAT) — the paper's lattice with $M\le n^{C}$

The milestone is stated for the code and lattice that the paper constructs, so it cannot be met by a construction whose targets depend on the instance in an arbitrary way; polynomial-time computability is not formalized.
